t: You're at Dorset Square, a garden square in Marylebone, lined entirely with listed terraced houses. Before the houses, this was the site of the Old Cricket Ground used by Lord's, which lasted until the 1811 season. The square is named for John Sackville, 3rd Duke of Dorset, a courtier and diplomat who was British Ambassador to France from 1784 and came home in 1789 as the Revolution escalated. Two other people connect here: the publisher George Bentley was born on the square, and Sir James Cantlie, a pioneer of first aid, died here.
